director.chapterArc: A quiet revelation of power followed by a strategic pivot and a somber, resolved departure.
director.restraintNote: The scene relies on stillness; avoid rushing the 'Reading' or the final realization about Rook's path. Let silence carry the weight of Dessa's tears and Toren's internal arithmetic.

cues.delivery: Dessa is demanding but protective; she needs Toren to witness the truth without embellishment.
cues.from: "Sit on that stone," she said. "Don't talk."
cues.through: "I said don't talk. I'm going to ask you for something in a minute and I want it done properly."
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional subtext.

cues.delivery: Toren is witnessing a phenomenon he cannot fully grasp; the tone should be hushed and reverent.
cues.from: "I was there," he said. "I watched it. It's not a thing you're remembering wrong and it's not a thing you've made better in your head. The dark got thinner. I was twelve feet away and I could see the stones on the far bank."

cues.delivery: Rook is clinical and precise; he treats the phenomenon as a fact to be measured.
cues.through: "It's —" Dessa blinked at it. "It's the same. It's exactly the same. It's a bit stiff because I've been sitting on wet grass since three in the morning."
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional subtext.

cues.delivery: Rook explains a technical concept; the delivery must be flat and instructional.
cues.from: "This is called a Reading," Rook said.
cues.through: "It's exactly a question. Don't improve it and don't be modest about it, because modesty is the single most common way of getting a Reading wrong." His fingers did not move. "Go in, look once, and say a fraction. Say the first one that arrives."
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional subtext.

cues.delivery: The revelation of 'Ember' status is delivered with absolute flatness; the emotion comes from Dessa's reaction.
cues.through: And Dessa Cole put her face in her hands and cried, in a wet field at first light, in front of exactly two people, and neither of them said one word about it then or afterward.
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional subtext.

cues.delivery: Wyck is factual; Ferrin is exhausted but clear. Maintain the rhythm of a tactical briefing.
cues.from: Wyck said, at the tailgate, in the voice he used for reading out a number: "You said you'd tell me first. In front of everybody. That's still on."
cues.through: "And I looked down at Ellet's Stage," she said, "and there's nine of them on it."
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional subtext.

cues.delivery: Senna is decisive; Rook is calculating. The dialogue should feel like a negotiation of survival.
cues.through: "Right," Rook said. "We're going north. Get the cart moving."
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional subtext.

cues.delivery: Rook reveals his motivation; the tone is weary but resolute.
cues.from: "There are two reasons and one of them is small," he said. "The small one is that I cannot come back from east. That isn't a feeling. It's a map. If I go, the six of you go north at seven miles a day with nobody in front of you, and I go east. There is no arrangement of days that ever puts me in front of you again before Meridian."
cues.through: They stopped at noon and he did the thing that cost.
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional subtext.

cues.delivery: Rook explains the chits; Ferrin responds with a mix of confusion and acceptance.
cues.from: "These are company pay-chits," Rook said. "They're not money. They're a mark of who's owed by whom. A factor or a yard-man or a ferry family who has seen one before will treat whoever's holding it as somebody worth talking to, and they will tell that person things they would never tell you."
cues.through: "I wasn't finished." She got her pack up. "My father asked what it was for. I've got an answer now and he'll hate it, because it isn't one."
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional subtext.

cues.delivery: Narrative observation of Rook's stillness; the tone should be observational and distant.
cues.from: Toren put the shafts down when Rook stopped, because everybody put the shafts down when Rook stopped.
cues.through: And then there was only a man standing on a rise with his hands at his sides at the end of a long day, not moving, for a length of time that nobody was ever going to be able to say.
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional subtext.

cues.delivery: Rook and Wyck coordinate; the tone is practical and physical.
cues.from: Then he took the near shaft out of Toren's hands.
cues.through: And the two of them took the cart up the north road at about four miles an hour, side by side, in the last of the light, with an old woman asleep in the bed of it and three children walking behind.
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional subtext.

cues.delivery: Toren's internal monologue; the tone is reflective and resigned.
cues.from: Toren watched the back of the man's head going away from him up the road.
cues.through: He had not said one word about it since. He was not going to. And he was going to pull that cart until the light went.
cues.reason: Character dialogue requiring specific emotional subtext.

pauses.reason: Revelation moment; pause for Rook's reaction to be felt before he speaks again.

pauses.after: "There. Done." Senna lay back down. "Put me on a floor with a roof on it. Take the cart and go and do the thing, and come back for me in a fortnight. And if I'm not there, I'm not there, and not one of you will have done a single thing wrong."
pauses.reason: Speaker reset and shift in dynamic as Senna makes her decision.

Dessa walked the head of the shafts and called the ground and did not once mention the thing she had done at three in the morning by a runnel, and Toren understood that this was going to be the shape of Dessa having something: she would keep it in a box and take it out when it was needed and never once show it to anybody for the pleasure of it.
pauses.reason: Completed thought; pause for Toren's observation of Dessa's restraint.
